subject: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
parts:
If we have...

foo <- reactiveValues(alist=list(a=1,b=2),blist=list(x=3,y=4));

You would expect that isolate(foo$alist <- as.list(1:3)) would prevent the invalidation of things that depend on foo$alist, analogously to how reading a variable wrapped in isolate prevents a dependency from being formed. Unfortunately, it does not.

My questions are:

* Is the effect of isolate(foo$alist <- as.list(1:3)) different in any way from the effect of foo$alist <- as.list(1:3) ?

* If there is a function which I want to update foo$alist silently (i.e. without triggering a cascade of invalidation) and there is another function where I do want the normal invalidation behavior on the same variable, is there a way to accomplish that without having to hunt down every observer that depends on foo$alist, and manually suspending it from within the first (silent) function?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
parts: No, there absolutely is not and it's hard for me to think of how you could reason about the system at all if we allowed such a thing. What is it you're trying to do?

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Re: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
parts: Example: an observer has a dependency on reactiveList value foo$bar. Under some conditions it writes to foo$bar (e.g. corrects a commonly occurring input error). There is no need for this observer to invalidate itself, though, because we already know the value of foo$bar and presumably acted on it. We want for it to "sit this round out" and wait for something else to update foo$bar and only then invalidate.

On Thursday, October 10, 2013 6:32:23 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
No, there absolutely is not and it's hard for me to think of how you could reason about the system at all if we allowed such a thing. What is it you're trying to do?

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Re: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
parts:
Aha!

I found a practical (albeit somewhat edge-casey) consequence of putting an assignment inside isolate() as currently implemented by shiny. The following adds a dynamically named log entry to a reactiveValues object (relog <- reactiveValues(log=list())):

isolate(relog$log[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one'));

...and somewhere else in the code you can print out the results in a table:

output$log <- renderTable(do.call(rbind,relog$log);

But the following causes whatever called it to go into an endless loop and bring the server to its knees:

relog$log[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one');

I think that the dynamic naming within a reactive object causes this statement to be interpreted as both a read and a write, creating a dependency loop. The fact that isolate() fixes it is how I must have gotten the mistaken idea that isolate does something similar for assign statements in general.

Interestingly, the following does not need isolate() to protect it from loops:

relog2 <- reactiveValues();
relog2[[as.character(Sys.time())]] <- c('c0001','Event one');
...
output$log <- renderTable(do.call(rbind,reactiveValuesToList(relog2)));
On Thursday, October 10, 2013 6:32:23 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
No, there absolutely is not and it's hard for me to think of how you could reason about the system at all if we allowed such a thing. What is it you're trying to do?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: A few questions about reactivity (part 2: assigning within an isolate statement)
parts: Yes, that's absolutely expected, though unfortunately not that intuitive, I'll admit! Assigning to subelements of values in reactiveValues will necessarily involve both a read and a write. For that reason I tend to write

relog$log <- log

instead. And indeed this kind of very imperative code needs to be wrapped in isolate!

I'll think about the "sit this round out" problem you mentioned.
